analysis.evidence: In יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת, God is the subject and לְיֶפֶת identifies the beneficiary: “May God give space to Japheth.” The verb יַפְתְּ echoes Japheth’s name, and the following וְיִשְׁכֹּן continues the blessing with another wish.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil jussive, third person masculine singular. The final ה of the root drops in this shortened form. There is no attached particle or pronominal suffix.
Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת, Noah asks God to make room for Japheth. The verb יַפְתְּ echoes the sound of the name יֶפֶת.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks Japheth as the beneficiary. יֶפֶת is a personal name.

analysis.evidence: בְּאָהֳלֵי שֵׁם gives the place of dwelling, “in the tents of Shem.” The surrounding wishes for Japheth and Canaan favor taking Japheth as the one who will dwell there, though אֱלֹהִים is also a possible subject.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the conjunction “and.” יִשְׁכֹּן is Qal, third-person masculine singular. Its form also fits the imperfect, but the blessing gives it jussive force.
analysis.sense: dwell or live in a place
